title: iodine session state and Notice evidence
description: Tracks version candidates, assigned user generations, exact DNS request and reply bindings, codec negotiation and bounded two way packet evidence. Completed DNS packets with matching ACKs or uniquely associated raw traffic qualify one CompatibleSession Notice per retained generation.

topics.title: Load the wire primitives into Iodine
topics.description: `@load ./wire` supplies DNSWire, byte slicing, codec decoding, zheader and the state limits. `module Iodine` places the records, pools and lifecycle functions in the shared Iodine namespace.

ranges.code:
@load ./wire
module Iodine;

topics.title: Retain fragment fingerprints and compact metadata
topics.description: Fragment starts with sequence sentinel 99 and poisoned=F. Four initially empty tables index each fragment number: hashes stores sha256_hash(body), lengths stores its byte count, starts stores its first two bytes, and finals stores the final flag. These fields retain the evidence used for completion and conflict checks.

topics.title: Initialize packet completion and acknowledgement state
topics.description: A fresh Fragment has complete=F, last=99, bytes=0 and acked=F. last identifies the final fragment after successful contiguous assembly; bytes records the qualifying packet length. up and down each receive an independent Fragment record.
links: Bind ACK to sequence and final fragment

topics.title: Keep generation identity and both packet directions
topics.description: Session requires client, server, suffix, assigned uid, epoch, version serial, version_token and touched time. login and downstream begin empty, upstream begins Base32 and done begins F. up and down each default to an empty Fragment. The default 32 fragment slots split into 16 upstream and 16 downstream slots.
links: Create the session from assigned candidate state
Apply the per direction slot bound

topics.title: Keep optional raw destination and directional evidence
topics.description: rawserver is an optional address established by an I reply. rawquery begins empty and stores a SHA256 fingerprint of a raw login challenge. rawpaired begins F; rawup and rawdown begin zero and retain the latest qualifying body length for each direction.
links: Read the observed raw server address

topics.title: Track version candidates and their FIFO links
topics.description: Candidate requires client, server, suffix, version serial, token and touched time. assigned=F, uid=99 and epoch=0 represent the initial version request. A matched VACK assigns a uid and generation. Empty prev and following strings mark queue boundaries.
links: Admit a candidate within its separate budget
Assign the returned user and generation

topics.title: Retain the minimal reply binding
topics.description: Pending stores command, suffix, client, server and born time. switch_value defaults empty and carries only the codec option needed by a reply. candidate and session default empty; epoch defaults zero. protected defaults F, with empty prev and following queue links. The request callback consumes login digests and encoded fragment bodies locally.
links: Retain only the codec switch value
Admit within the shared pending budget

topics.title: Own candidates, pending transactions and sessions separately
topics.description: Three string keyed tables own Candidate, Pending and Session records. Each table has its own configured bound: candidate_limit defaults 256, pending_limit defaults 1024 and session_limit defaults 256. Assigned version candidates stay in candidates until login promotion or replacement; progressed sessions consume the session pool.

topics.title: Separate candidate FIFO and both pending classes
topics.description: chead and ctail delimit the candidate FIFO. phead and ptail each map F and T to their own pending FIFO boundaries. `p$protected` chooses the class. serial orders version observations; generation assigns distinct accepted VACK epochs.
links: Append within the selected pending class

topics.title: Track occupancy peaks and resource outcomes
topics.description: pending_peak, candidate_peak and session_peak start at zero. degraded counts capacity eviction or refused admission, rejected_large records oversized input in the entry module, and integrity_errors counts broken queue invariants. The exit aggregate reports all six counters alongside current occupancy.

ranges.code:
global pending_peak: count=0; global candidate_peak: count=0; global session_peak: count=0;
global degraded: count=0; global rejected_large: count=0; global integrity_errors: count=0;

topics.title: Update the three occupancy high water marks
topics.description: peaks compares each owning table size with its retained maximum. Successful pending and candidate admission and session creation call this helper, so the counters capture peak simultaneous records in each pool.

topics.title: Resolve pending membership and its protected class
topics.description: premove requires the key to exist. A missing key increments integrity_errors and returns. For a present record, the helper reads its protected flag to select the matching head and tail table entries.

topics.title: Unlink pending records with fixed adjacent updates
topics.description: Removal patches the preceding record or class head, then the following record or class tail, and deletes pending[key]. A missing referenced neighbor increments integrity_errors. Each removal touches a fixed number of links; callers that find records by expiry or session identity still scan bounded tables.
links: Find pending records owned by a session

topics.title: Resolve a candidate before unlinking it
topics.description: cremove requires candidate membership, increments integrity_errors for a missing key and reads the Candidate record used for its adjacent links.

topics.title: Repair the candidate FIFO around a removed entry
topics.description: The helper updates a preceding candidate or chead and a following candidate or ctail, then deletes the record. Missing referenced neighbors increment integrity_errors. Head eviction and login promotion reuse this fixed set of link updates.
links: Evict the oldest candidate at capacity

topics.title: Prepare removal of a retained session generation
topics.description: sinvalidate returns for an absent session. For a retained key, a local vector collects pending keys whose session field refers to that key. Pending records preserve their admission epoch until removal.

topics.title: Scan pending bindings before deleting a session
topics.description: A full scan of the bounded pending table collects every transaction bound to key. A second pass calls premove for each collected key, preserving both FIFO classes while the table changes. The final delete releases the Session and its fragment metadata.

topics.title: Expire pending transactions by network time
topics.description: expire samples network_time() once. It scans pending and selects entries whose age from born reaches pending_ttl_seconds, which defaults 30secs. A local vector separates selection from mutation; premove releases each selected record and its FIFO links.

topics.title: Expire candidates from their last version progress
topics.description: The reused removal vector selects candidates whose touched age reaches candidate_ttl_seconds, default 30secs. cremove then releases the selected records. A VACK refreshes touched; an exact repeated request preserves the existing candidate record.

topics.title: Expire idle sessions and their pending bindings
topics.description: The session scan selects touched ages at least session_idle_seconds, default 300secs. sinvalidate removes each selected session and its pending transactions. A completed Session keeps done and generation deduplication for its retained lifetime; qualifying later traffic refreshes touched.

topics.title: Protect session pending entries under capacity pressure
topics.description: padd preserves an existing key. pending_limit=0 refuses admission and increments degraded. At capacity, phead[F] selects the oldest unprotected pending transaction for eviction; a table containing only protected entries refuses the new admission. Both eviction and refusal increment degraded. The default shared limit is 1024.
links: Append admitted state to its class

topics.title: Append a pending transaction to its admission class
topics.description: p$protected selects a FIFO. The new record stores its previous tail, updates that tail record or the class head, becomes ptail[pool], and enters pending. peaks updates occupancy after admission. These assignments change a fixed number of links.
links: Protect pending commands for a session

topics.title: Bound version candidates independently of sessions
topics.description: cadd preserves an existing candidate key. A zero candidate_limit refuses with degraded incremented. At the default limit of 256, cremove(chead) evicts the oldest retained candidate and increments degraded. Candidate pressure uses the candidate pool while progressed sessions retain their separate budget.

topics.title: Append candidates through the retained tail
topics.description: The new candidate stores ctail in prev. The previous tail gains a following link, or chead becomes the new key for an empty queue. ctail, candidates[key] and occupancy peaks then update. Promotion and expiry repair the same embedded links.

topics.title: Key sessions by peers, suffix and assigned user
topics.description: skey formats client, server, suffix and uid with pipe separators. A session therefore persists across DNS source port changes while retaining the observed peer pair, suffix and assigned user context. epoch separately identifies a retained generation.

ranges.code:
function skey(client: addr, server: addr, suffix: string, uid: count): string
{ return fmt("%s|%s|%s|%d",client,server,suffix,uid); }

links: Bind each DNS transaction to both ports

topics.title: Bind DNS replies to ports, ID and the exact question
topics.description: pkey includes client, server, cp, sp, d$id and sha256_hash(d$question). DNSWire.question contains the expanded label bytes with their original spelling plus qtype and qclass bytes. Request and response must produce this exact tuple to share pending state.

ranges.code:
function pkey(client: addr, server: addr, cp: port, sp: port, d: DNSWire): string
{ return fmt("%s|%s|%s|%s|%d|%s",client,server,cp,sp,d$id,sha256_hash(d$question)); }

links: Key version candidates by exact question fingerprint

topics.title: Admit a normalized suffix with explicit syntax
topics.description: suffix_ok requires a nonempty suffix whose first character is a lowercase letter, digit or underscore. Remaining characters may also include dots and hyphens. The version request constructs the lowercase suffix before applying this predicate.

ranges.code:
function suffix_ok(s: string): bool
{ return |s|>0 && /^[a-z0-9_][a-z0-9_.-]*$/ == s; }

topics.title: Find a stored suffix and concatenate command labels
topics.description: prefix_for tries suffix boundaries starting after the first label. It lowercases the joined suffix for comparison and returns the preceding labels concatenated with an empty separator. Exhausting the bounded name returns an empty prefix. Later command checks validate the prefix shape.
links: Resolve command context against observed peers

topics.title: Bound the login metadata text and split its fields
topics.description: login_ok bounds the body at 80 bytes and requires four hyphen separated fields shaped as two dotted numeric addresses followed by two decimal numbers. split_string must return exactly four fields before address validation starts.
links: Validate address octets and numeric ranges

topics.title: Validate the login address octets and numeric fields
topics.description: The first two fields each require four decimal octets, each one to three characters and at most 255. The third field must be 1 through 65535 and the fourth 1 through 32. The accepted body becomes the literal login metadata in the Notice sub field.

topics.title: Bound fragment slots and reset on a new sequence
topics.description: fragment preserves the current record for an empty body or a fragment index at least 16 or bounded_fragment_slots_per_session/2. The default 32 slots allow 16 per direction. A changed sequence replaces the Fragment with a fresh record. A poisoned record returns early; accepted bodies receive a SHA256 fingerprint.

topics.title: Poison a sequence when repeated evidence conflicts
topics.description: For an already retained fragment index, the body fingerprint and final flag must equal the first evidence. A conflict sets poisoned=T and clears complete and acked. An identical repeat returns the existing metadata. A later sequence change creates fresh state.
links: Count ACK only for a complete packet

topics.title: Store length, first two bytes and final flag
topics.description: A new slot retains sha256_hash(body), its byte length, at most the first two bytes through cut, and its final flag. The full decoded body stays local to the callback. These bounded tables support duplicate detection, total length and zheader qualification.

ranges.code: f$hashes[frag]=hash; f$lengths[frag]=|body|; f$starts[frag]=cut(body,0,|body|<2 ? |body| : 2); f$finals[frag]=final;

links: Reconstruct only length and header bytes

topics.title: Clear packet evidence whenever a new fragment arrives
topics.description: Every newly retained fragment clears complete and acked, resets last to 99 and bytes to zero, then initializes local assembly metadata. This also requalifies a packet that had already completed or received an ACK when an additional fragment changes its evidence.

topics.title: Walk consecutive slots from fragment zero
topics.description: The loop advances only while the next index exists and is below 16. It sums lengths and collects at most two leading bytes across fragments. The first final flag records last and ends the walk. A missing index stops assembly before later retained fragments.
links: Require an exact final slot count

topics.title: Qualify an exact contiguous packet with zheader
topics.description: Completion requires a final fragment, exactly last+1 retained slots and zheader(head,bytes). zheader requires at least two header bytes, total length at least 8, compression method 8, window value at most 7, header word divisible by 31 and the dictionary flag clear. Success stores complete, last and total bytes.
links: Bind the peer ACK to this completed packet

topics.title: Bind acknowledgement to sequence and final fragment
topics.description: ack sets acked=T only when the Fragment is complete and its sequence and last fragment equal the supplied ACK fields. Request and reply paths extract those fields from their respective headers. A new fragment or conflicting duplicate clears the earlier acknowledgement.

ranges.code:
function ack(f: Fragment, seq: count, frag: count): Fragment
{ if (f$complete && f$seq==seq && f$last==frag) f$acked=T; return f; }

links: Read upstream fragment and downstream ACK bits
Read downstream fragment and upstream ACK bits
Require both completed ACK bound directions

topics.title: Require login and qualified traffic for one retained generation
topics.description: maybe_notice requires a retained session with done=F and nonempty login. The raw branch requires rawpaired, positive rawup and rawdown lengths and an assigned rawserver. The DNS branch requires complete and acked in both up and down. These guards select the evidence used to construct Iodine::CompatibleSession.
links: Select the transport and directional values

topics.title: Select the exact transport, codecs and counts
topics.description: DNS output takes bytes and last+1 fragment counts from up and down, codecs from upstream and downstream, transport=dns and dst=server. Raw output substitutes rawup and rawdown, one fragment per direction, Raw codecs, transport=raw and rawserver as dst.
links: Read the literal message and sub format

topics.title: Emit the literal message and ordered evidence fields
topics.description: NOTICE selects CompatibleSession. msg is the fixed session pattern text. sub formats evidence=version,login,data_up,data_down followed by transport, suffix, assigned user, both codecs, literal version=0x00000502, login metadata, both byte counts and both fragment counts. src is client, dst is the selected observed server, and identifier combines the session key with epoch.

ranges.code:
NOTICE([$note=CompatibleSession,
$msg="iodine session pattern observed: matched negotiation followed by two way tunnel traffic",
$sub=fmt("evidence=version,login,data_up,data_down;transport=%s;suffix=%s;userid=%d;upstream=%s;downstream=%s;version=0x00000502;login=%s;up_bytes=%d;down_bytes=%d;up_fragments=%d;down_fragments=%d",transport,s$suffix,s$uid,uc,dc,s$login,up,down,uf,df),
$src=s$client,$dst=dst,$identifier=fmt("%s|epoch=%d",key,s$epoch)]);

topics.title: Keep the emitted flag in the retained Session
topics.description: After NOTICE, sessions[key]$done becomes T. Both transport paths share this flag, yielding one emission per retained generation. The Session remains in its bounded pool with its deduplication state until idle expiry or generation replacement; qualifying traffic can refresh its idle time.

ranges.code:
sessions[key]$done=T;
}

links: Replace a generation after a newer VACK

topics.title: Build a transaction token before parsing the wire command
topics.description: request requires at least two labels and computes the exact peer, port, DNS ID and question token. A retained token returns immediately. The first character of the first label becomes the lowercase wire command used throughout context lookup.
links: Normalize data only after scanning peers

topics.title: Validate version 1282 and derive the candidate identity
topics.description: A v request requires an 11 character first label. Its ten encoded characters must decode as six Base32 bytes with the first four equal to 1282, the 0x00000502 version. The remaining labels form a valid lowercase suffix. ct combines client, server, suffix and the exact question fingerprint.

topics.title: Preserve exact version retransmissions and admit pending VACK
topics.description: A scan of retained sessions finds any matching version_token and returns for that exact version request. Otherwise serial advances and cadd admits or preserves ct. An existing ct keeps its first Candidate serial and generation. padd retains an unprotected v transaction pointing to ct; candidate and pending admission use separate bounds.

topics.title: Search retained sessions within the observed peer pair
topics.description: The session scan first matches client and server, then finds that session suffix in the current labels. Each candidate context receives fresh decoded and id locals. A matching context supplies the prefix used by later command processing. This is a full scan bounded by session_limit.
links: Decode a user while preserving the wire command

topics.title: Resolve each command family to the assigned user
topics.description: l, p and n decode the prefix after its command as Base32 and read the first byte as id. i, s and o read the next Base32 character as id. A hexadecimal first character supplies the data userid directly. The first session whose uid equals id supplies sid, prefix and uid; cmd keeps its wire value throughout the scan.
links: Rename data after the full scan

topics.title: Rename hexadecimal data after peer lookup
topics.description: After every possible session context has been examined, a hexadecimal wire command becomes data. Delaying this assignment lets each shared peer userid comparison inspect the same original hexadecimal command.

ranges.code:
# Keep the wire command unchanged while every possible userid is scanned.
if (/^[0-9a-f]$/ == cmd) cmd="data";

links: Inspect each user with the immutable wire command

topics.title: Choose the newest matching assigned login candidate
topics.description: For l with sid empty, the bounded candidate scan requires assigned state and the observed client and server. A matching suffix must leave a 32 character prefix. Its 31 Base32 payload characters must decode to 19 bytes with the assigned userid first. The greatest matching Candidate serial wins.

topics.title: Promote assigned state within the session budget
topics.description: The chosen Candidate supplies suffix and uid for skey. A new key at session_limit, default 256, increments degraded and returns. Admission creates Session with the Candidate epoch, serial and token, refreshes touched, removes the Candidate through cremove and updates peaks. Its field defaults initialize codecs, fragments, raw evidence and done.

topics.title: Require session context and a valid command stage
topics.description: Processing continues for a retained sid. l must decode to 19 Base32 bytes with the session uid in its first byte. Other commands require accepted login metadata. The command set admits l, i, s, o, p, data and n for the established context.
links: Bind an eligible command to this epoch

topics.title: Keep the codec option and protect the transaction epoch
topics.description: Only s or o with a seven character prefix retains cut(prefix,2,1) as switch_value. padd stores command, suffix, observed peers, born time, sid and the current epoch with protected=T. Successful admission refreshes touched. Pending retains this small option while login digests and fragment payloads remain local.
links: Check the retained epoch on reply
Preserve protected pending entries under pressure

topics.title: Decode upstream data using the negotiated codec
topics.description: data requires at least five prefix characters and a selected downstream codec. Three header characters must map to Base32 values at most 31. The payload beginning at offset 5 decodes with sess$upstream; an unsuccessful decode returns before fragment and ACK changes.

topics.title: Apply downstream ACK and upstream fragment coordinates
topics.description: The request acknowledges downstream sequence b%8 and final fragment e/2. It feeds upstream sequence a/4, fragment (a%4)*4+b/8 and final flag e%2==1 to fragment with the decoded body. The p branch handles a separate compact acknowledgement shape.

topics.title: Decode the ping ACK and evaluate DNS evidence
topics.description: An eight character p prefix decodes its seven payload characters as Base32. Four decoded bytes with the assigned uid first acknowledge downstream sequence (byte1/16)%8 and fragment byte1%16. After request processing, maybe_notice(sid,F) evaluates the DNS completion guards.

topics.title: Consume the exact pending transaction before reply handling
topics.description: response recomputes pkey and requires pending membership. It copies the Pending record, unlinks it through premove and then requires a valid decoded answer. body, sid and codec locals drive command handling. A matching reply consumes its pending token even when its answer fails later command checks.
links: Bind peers, ports and exact question

topics.title: Accept a bounded VACK and a newer version serial
topics.description: The v branch requires its Candidate to remain present, a nine byte body beginning VACK and an assigned byte at offset 8 at most 15. The observed peers, Candidate suffix and returned uid determine sid. For an existing sid, the Candidate serial must exceed the retained Session serial.
links: Reset an existing session for a newer version

topics.title: Assign a fresh generation to the returned userid
topics.description: Each accepted VACK increments generation and writes assigned=T, the returned uid and the new epoch into its Candidate. touched refreshes to network_time(). A new session key leaves this assigned Candidate ready for login promotion.
links: Select the assigned candidate for login

topics.title: Replace an existing user generation after newer VACK
topics.description: For an already retained sid, sinvalidate first removes that Session and every pending reference to it. The replacement Session receives the new epoch, Candidate serial and version token with fresh defaults. cremove releases the Candidate and peaks updates occupancy. The version reply then returns.
links: Scan and unlink the old pending references

topics.title: Require the session and its pending admission epoch
topics.description: Every established command reply requires sid to remain in sessions and p$epoch to equal sessions[sid]$epoch. A replacement generation therefore requires pending state admitted for that same generation before reply processing continues.

ranges.code:
if (sid !in sessions || p$epoch!=sessions[sid]$epoch) return;
local s=sessions[sid];

links: Capture the epoch when admitting the request

topics.title: Store login metadata and select the initial downstream codec
topics.description: The l reply must pass login_ok before its body becomes `sessions[sid]$login`. NULL qtype 10 and PRIVATE qtype 65399 select Raw downstream bytes. Other carriers take d$answer$codec from the decoded wire answer. Subsequent command branches require retained login metadata.

topics.title: Read the IPv4 raw destination from the I reply
topics.description: A paired i reply beginning I supplies rawserver only when its body is exactly five bytes. bytestring_to_count and count_to_v4_addr convert the following four bytes into the observed raw server address.

ranges.code:
else if (p$command=="i" && cut(body,0,1)=="I") {
if (|body|==5) sessions[sid]$rawserver=count_to_v4_addr(bytestring_to_count(cut(body,1,4)));

links: Associate a raw packet with exactly one session

topics.title: Accept an echoed upstream codec selection
topics.description: For s with a retained switch_value, b32val maps 5 to Base32, 6 to Base64, 26 to Base64u and 7 to Base128. The response body must equal the selected codec string before upstream changes.
links: Decode later data with the selected upstream codec

topics.title: Require option, response text and carrier codec agreement
topics.description: For o, the lowercase option maps t to Base32, s to Base64, u to Base64u, v to Base128 and r to Raw. downstream changes only when a mapped codec equals both the body text and d$answer$codec.
links: Require the selected codec on data replies

topics.title: Decode reply ACK bits and downstream fragment metadata
topics.description: A p or data reply requires at least two bytes, a selected downstream codec, matching d$answer$codec and a first byte at least 128. Byte zero acknowledges upstream sequence (byte0/16)%8 and final fragment byte0%16. Byte one supplies downstream sequence byte1/32, fragment (byte1/2)%16 and final bit byte1%2==1. The remaining bytes enter fragment. Processing refreshes touched and evaluates DNS Notice guards.

topics.title: Read the raw magic, userid and command nibble
topics.description: rawpacket requires four bytes and the prefix 0x10 0xd1 0x9e. The low nibble of byte three supplies uid; the high nibble supplies command as a multiple of 16. chosen and matches begin empty and zero before association.

topics.title: Require a unique logged in raw peer and user association
topics.description: The bounded session scan counts records matching client, assigned rawserver, raw server address, uid and nonempty login. Exactly one match supplies chosen. The body starts after the four byte raw header. Ambiguous associations return before raw state changes.
links: Assign the raw server from a paired reply

topics.title: Pair a request and distinct reply challenge fingerprint
topics.description: Command 16 with a 16 byte body records sha256_hash(body) as rawquery in the upstream direction. A downstream challenge with a retained request fingerprint and a different SHA256 fingerprint sets rawpaired=T. This comparison uses SHA256 as a compact equality fingerprint and records a distinct request and reply challenge pair used by the raw traffic guard.

topics.title: Record bounded raw data in both directions
topics.description: Command 32 requires total payload at most 4096 bytes, rawpaired and zheader(body,|body|). zheader requires a body length at least 8 and the supported compression header structure. The current direction stores its body length in rawup or rawdown. Command 48 requires exactly the four byte header. Accepted handling refreshes touched and maybe_notice(chosen,T) requires positive data lengths from both directions.
links: Require the complete raw evidence set

topics.title: Prepare bounded queue diagnostics
topics.description: integrity starts with an empty visited set, chead as current, an empty previous key and count zero. The candidate and pending traversals validate the actual links retained by admission and removal.

topics.title: Check candidate membership, back links, count and tail
topics.description: The candidate walk is bounded by the owning table size. A missing or repeated key increments integrity_errors and stops the walk. Each prev must equal the previous key. Final checks require the visited count to equal candidates size, previous to equal ctail and current to be empty. The visited set then resets for pending diagnostics.

topics.title: Walk both pending FIFO classes with a shared visited set
topics.description: For each phead class, the traversal begins at its head and bounds iterations by pending size. Every key must exist and appear once across both chains. Each prev must match the preceding key, and protected must equal the selected pool. The walk advances through following while counting visits.
links: Compare tails and complete table coverage
Link admission into its protected class

topics.title: Require each pending tail and full table coverage
topics.description: Each class walk must end at its ptail with an empty current link. After both classes, the visited set size must equal pending table size. These checks catch orphaned entries and inconsistent queue boundaries through integrity_errors.

topics.title: Schedule expiry at the configured one second interval
topics.description: sweep calls expire and schedules another sweep when sweep_interval_seconds is positive. zeek_init schedules the first event under the same condition. The default interval is 1secs. Each expiry pass scans bounded owning tables; session removal can additionally scan pending bindings.

topics.title: Run final expiry and queue integrity checks
topics.description: zeek_done calls expire and integrity before printing the aggregate health record. Expiry uses network_time() and the configured TTLs. A recent done Session remains retained when its idle age is below session_idle_seconds.

topics.title: Print one IODINE_HEALTH aggregate at exit
topics.description: The print writes IODINE_HEALTH followed by a JSON object containing the three occupancy peaks, three final table sizes, degraded, rejected_large and integrity_errors. Final occupancy reflects the preceding expiry pass. The aggregate provides resource and queue diagnostics alongside Notice output.

ranges.code:
print fmt("IODINE_HEALTH {\"pending_peak\":%d,\"candidate_peak\":%d,\"session_peak\":%d,\"pending_final\":%d,\"candidate_final\":%d,\"session_final\":%d,\"degraded\":%d,\"rejected_large\":%d,\"integrity_errors\":%d}",pending_peak,candidate_peak,session_peak,|pending|,|candidates|,|sessions|,degraded,rejected_large,integrity_errors);
}

links: Run the final cleanup and checks

topics.title: Follow version assignment through pending epoch binding
topics.description: A newer accepted VACK assigns generation to the Candidate. Login promotion copies its epoch into Session, request admission copies that epoch into Pending, and the reply guard compares it against the current Session. Replacing an existing session first removes all pending references to the old generation.

ranges.code: sessions[sid]=[$client=client,$server=server,$suffix=admitted$suffix,$uid=admitted$uid,$epoch=admitted$epoch,$serial=admitted$serial,$version_token=admitted$token,$touched=network_time()];
if (!padd(token,[$command=cmd,$suffix=sess$suffix,$switch_value=switch_value,$client=client,$server=server,$born=network_time(),$session=sid,$epoch=sess$epoch,$protected=T])) return;
if (sid !in sessions || p$epoch!=sessions[sid]$epoch) return;

topics.title: Follow new evidence through completion and ACK qualification
topics.description: Compact fragment metadata records fingerprints, lengths, leading bytes and final flags. Every new slot clears completion and acknowledgement. The contiguous exact slot count and zheader checks rebuild completion; ack then requires that exact packet sequence and final fragment. Both directions must qualify before DNS emission.

ranges.code: f$hashes[frag]=hash; f$lengths[frag]=|body|; f$starts[frag]=cut(body,0,|body|<2 ? |body| : 2); f$finals[frag]=final;
f$complete=F; f$acked=F; f$last=99; f$bytes=0;
if (last!=99 && |f$hashes|==last+1 && zheader(head,bytes)) { f$complete=T; f$last=last; f$bytes=bytes; }
{ if (f$complete && f$seq==seq && f$last==frag) f$acked=T; return f; }
else if (!s$up$complete || !s$down$complete || !s$up$acked || !s$down$acked) return;

links: Reset on each newly retained fragment

topics.title: Separate fixed link maintenance from bounded scans
topics.description: Admission appends through retained tails and removal patches adjacent links. Expiry still scans each bounded table, sinvalidate scans pending to collect session references, and command resolution scans retained contexts. Protected pending entries use their own FIFO while capacity eviction selects phead[F]. These are distinct operations with distinct bounds.

ranges.code: for (p in pending) if (now-pending[p]$born>=pending_ttl_seconds) remove[|remove|]=p;
for (p in pending) if (pending[p]$session==key) remove[|remove|]=p;

topics.title: Follow unique association into raw evidence output
topics.description: Raw handling first selects exactly one session matching the observed peer and assigned user. A 16 byte challenge request fingerprint and a distinct reply fingerprint set rawpaired. Bounded zheader qualified command 32 bodies supply both directional lengths; the shared Notice guard and done flag control emission for the retained generation.

ranges.code: if (ss$client==client && ss?$rawserver && ss$rawserver==server && ss$uid==uid && ss$login!="") { chosen=candidate_session; ++matches; }
